text:
The air in the interrogation room was thick enough to choke on. Detective Miller leaned forward, his elbows resting on the scarred metal table, eyes locked onto the trembling man across from him.

"Let's try this again," Miller said, his voice low and steady, cutting through the hum of the fluorescent lights. "Where were you the night of the crime?"

The suspect, a young man with sweat beading on his forehead, shifted in his chair. He wouldn't meet the detective's gaze, instead staring at his own knuckles, which were white from gripping his knees.

"I was home," he stammered, his voice cracking. "All night. I swear it, I didn't move from my couch."

Miller didn't blink. He knew the truth was hiding somewhere in the gaps between those words. He needed to break through the panic.

"Name the shape with three sides."
